scope: Review of ISO 32000-2:2020 Annex I (I.1-I.3) and Annex K (K.1-K.2), effective EC3 context, current ledger/code/assertions, and directly relevant ADR decisions. No general Annex E audit, no repeated BX/EX or media cases, and no claim of full XFA 3.3 conformance.

source_pages.annex_i: PDF physical pp. 951-952; printed pp. 936-937 (physical p. 953 / printed p. 938 begins Annex J and is outside scope)
source_pages.errata: No direct Annex I or Annex K issue appears in doc/errata-read.md. Rendered primary pages 951-952 and 959-961 show no visible EC3 correction overlay. Issue #399 is a §7.7.2 catalog-version amendment relevant to I.2's version chain, not an Annex I erratum.

features.rule: Processor may ignore or inform about an object it does not understand; the choice is per feature and discretionary.
features.assessment: Two contrasting reader choices are exercised end-to-end: unknown image filter is named while understood fill draws; unknown page-dictionary key is silently passed over while both marks draw. This is selected evidence for the discretionary rule, not proof for all features.

features.rule: Use the PDF version stated by the file (header/catalog, including cumulative revisions); a processor shall attempt to read a file newer than it supports.
features.source: physical pp. 951-952 / printed pp. 936-937; §7.7.2 Issue #399 governs catalog version across updates
features.assessment: The effective version is numeric and the reader does not gate opening on it. The strict PDF 2.1 fixture is parsed without recovery, opens, draws a black fill, then can be reported. This proves a bounded read attempt, not arbitrary future-feature support.

features.rule: On a newer version or unprocessable document requirement, SHOULD warn both that reading may fail and that changing/saving may be unavailable. SHOULD notify on the first unrecognized-feature error and suppress later such errors; continue where possible.
features.assessment: The version and unmet-requirement messages carry both warning clauses. The first-error suppression recommendation is intentionally declined: all unrecognized features remain reported as structured items; the owner adopted that choice in doc/questions/A834 item 4 and ADR 2815 §2. The exception classes in the source (I/O, memory, command failure) are therefore not the basis for a global suppression claim.

features.rule: Writer SHOULD preserve a source version newer than it supports; MAY raise an older version if it writes newer features; when inserting another PDF, SHOULD use the newer input version.
features.assessment: Incremental update preserves source bytes/header, insertion raises catalog /Version to the greater effective input version, and archive has a named PDF/A-4 conversion exception retaining source history. The optional bump where newer features are added is not an independent duty absent such a writer case.

features.rule: Unknown entries in existing dictionaries can be ignored as absent. Some features cannot be ignored and give little choice but error; some features can degrade silently. These are descriptive compatibility cases, not a universal command to reject or report all unknown input.
features.assessment: The existing assertion set includes passed-over dictionary data, an unsupported object report, and feature-specific fallback/report cases. It does not certify all silently degraded or impossible-to-ignore features.

features.rule: Annex K is deprecated in PDF 2.0. An interactive processor supporting XFA shall clearly identify interaction with an XFA form. A processor may choose not to implement schema-driven page generation; whether generated pages are materialized is implementation-dependent.
features.assessment: A checked-in hybrid PDF opens on the normal viewer path, and the host's Report receives a clear XFA identity plus the AcroForm/XFA behavior actually carried out. Dynamic XFA page generation is accepted and scheduled after ledger work by ADR 2876, but not yet built; the report identifies the currently exercised interim K.1 permission to omit it. Current policy does not silently claim generated layout.

features.rule: XFA is an XML stream or packet array. The resource carries template/data/config information. When creating or modifying XFA PDF, a writer keeps AcroForm entries consistent, includes field objects, maps names through XFA SOM, keeps field /V and XFA data consistent, and avoids field annotation /A or /AA where XFA supplies actions.
assertions: crates/pdf-model/tests/xfa_datasets.rs (checked-in hybrid corpus edits and reopen assertions)
features.assessment: Both resource encodings are read; hybrid field data is kept consistent on save, with reported limits. The corpus and authored-form tests assert actual values, calculations, validations, and host reporting. The PDF clause's writer constraints apply when those writer operations occur; they are not a reader-side requirement to reject a nonconforming hybrid. The audit does not claim all external XFA 3.3 behavior.

ledger_mapping.current_status: All seven rows are marked implemented in doc/conformance/ledger.toml. I and K aggregate their child rows. K.2's implementation is scoped by the static XFA ratification and the explicit dynamic-layout permission; dynamic generation is accepted and scheduled after ledger work, but not yet built; it is not a certification of the entire XFA 3.3 specification.
ledger_mapping.traceability: doc/reviews/1983-specification-audit/features.json still has stale earlier I.2 warning notes in some records; the current ledger and ADR 2815 reflect the repaired two-part notices and the completed insertion-version rule. Annex E.1's older cross-reference still calls first-error suppression unreviewed, while current evidence documents the owner-approved departure.

execution: No Cargo commands run. Existing assertions and code were read; test pass/fail status is not inferred from names.
